For as the farmer sows many seeds on the ground and sets out a multitude of plants, and yet not everything sown comes up safely in due season, nor does everything planted take root, so too not all those who have been sown in the world will be saved.”
I replied, “If I have found grace, let me speak.
If the farmer’s seed does not sprout, or does not receive your rain in due season, or if it is ruined by too much rain, it perishes.{l}
But man, who was formed by your hands and is called your image because he is made like you, and for whose sake you have formed all things, have you made him like the farmer’s seed?{m}
Do not be angry with us, but spare your people and have mercy on your inheritance; for you have mercy on your own creation.”
He replied, “Things present are for those now present, and things to come for those to come.
For you come far short of being able to love my creation more than I do. But I have often drawn near to you yourself, though never to the unrighteous.{n}
And in this also you are admirable before the Most High,
in that you have humbled yourself, as befits you, and have not counted yourself among the righteous so as to be greatly glorified.
For many grievous miseries will befall those who inhabit the world in the last times, because they have walked in great pride.
But as for you, understand for yourself, and seek out glory for those like you.

For it is for you that paradise has been opened, the tree of life planted, the age to come made ready, plenty provided, a city built, rest appointed,{o} goodness perfected, and wisdom brought to completion.
The root of evil has been sealed up from you; weakness and the moth{p} have been hidden from you, and corruption has fled into the underworld to be forgotten.
Sorrows have passed away, and at the end the treasure of immortality has been made manifest.
So ask no more questions about the multitude of those who perish.
For they too received freedom, but they scorned the Most High, held his law in contempt, and forsook his ways.
Moreover, they have trampled on his righteous ones,
and have told themselves in their hearts, ‘God does not exist,’ though they knew well they must die.
For just as the things foretold will welcome you, so thirst and torment, which have been prepared, will await them. For he did not wish anyone to be destroyed;
but those who were created have themselves defiled the name of him who made them, and have been ungrateful to him who prepared life for them.
That is why my judgment is now drawing near.
These things I have not shown to all, but only to you and a few like you.”
Then I replied,{q} “Look, lord, you have now shown me a host of signs which you will begin to perform in the last times, but you have not shown me at what time.”

The meaning of “fire and water” is uncertain; perhaps the warmth and fluid of the womb.
The Latin of this verse is obscure.
Latin “it is easy by your command to arrange that what was made be preserved”; the rendering follows the sense reported in the oriental versions.
Latin “the swiftness of the judge who is to come.”

The words are a heading within the text; many Latin manuscripts and the oriental versions reportedly have them. Ezra’s being “taken up” is described in 14:9, 49–50 (in the oriental versions; see 14:48 note).
Latin “who inhabit the world (or the age)”; the oriental versions reportedly read “who abide for ever,” and the Latin may reflect a confusion of the two senses of Hebrew olam, “age, eternity, world.”
Compare Psalm 104:4. The oriental versions reportedly read, “at whose command they are changed to wind and fire.”
Latin “and truth bears witness”; the oriental versions reportedly read, “whose truth endures for ever.”
That is, the faithful who confess God.
The Latin of verse 43 lacks a main verb; the words “it perishes” are taken from the first word of verse 44 (sic periit, “so it perishes”).
The Latin is confused; the rendering follows the sense reported in the oriental versions. Compare Genesis 1:26–27.
Latin “I have often drawn near to you and to yourself, but never to the unrighteous”; the oriental versions reportedly read, “you have often compared yourself to the unrighteous. Never do so!”
Latin probata, “approved,” perhaps “appointed.”
Latin tinea, “moth” or “worm,” an image of decay; the oriental versions reportedly read “death.”
In the Clementine Latin the words “Then I replied” stand at the end of verse 62; they are placed here at the start of verse 63.

verses.text: He replied, “Measure the time carefully within yourself; and when you see that a certain part of the signs foretold has gone by,
you will know that this is the hour at which the Most High will begin to visit the world of his making.
And when there appear in the world quakings of places, tumult of peoples,{a}
then you will understand that it was of these things the Most High spoke, from the days that were before you, from the beginning.
For just as everything made in the world has a beginning and likewise a completion, and the completion is plain to see,
so too the times of the Most High have beginnings plain to see in portents and mighty acts, and completions in deeds and in signs.
And it shall be that everyone who is saved, and who is able to escape by his works, or by the faith with which you have believed,{b}
will be left alive out of the perils foretold, and will see my salvation in my land and within my borders, which I have consecrated for myself from eternity.
Then those who have now misused my ways will be in anguish,{c} and those who have cast them aside with contempt will abide in torments.
For those who did not acknowledge me while they lived, though they received my benefits,
and those who loathed my law while they still had freedom,
and who, while room for repentance was still open to them, did not understand but scorned it, these must come to know it after death, in torment.
So do not go on being curious as to how the ungodly will be tormented; rather inquire how the righteous will be saved, whose the world is, for whom the world exists, and when.”
I replied,
“I said it before, I say it now, and I will say it again: those who perish are more than those who will be saved,
as a wave is greater than a drop.”

He replied,{d} “As the field is, so are the seeds; as the flowers are, so are their colors; as the worker is, so is the product; and as the farmer is, so is his tillage. For it was the time of the world.{e}
When I was preparing the world for those who now exist, before it was made for them to dwell in, no one opposed me;{f}
for no one then existed. But now those who have been created in this world that was prepared, with its unfailing harvest and its unsearchable law, have become corrupt in their ways.
Then I looked upon my world, and there it lay ruined; my earth was in danger through the schemes of those who had come into it.{g}
And I saw and spared some, though with great difficulty, and kept for myself one grape out of a cluster, and one plant out of a great forest.{h}
So let the multitude perish which was born in vain, and let my grape be saved, and my plant; for with much labor I have brought them to perfection.
“Now, if you will let yet another seven days pass—but do not fast in them;
rather go into a field of flowers where no house has been built, and eat only of the flowers of the field; taste no meat and drink no wine, but only flowers—
and pray to the Most High without ceasing; and I will come and speak with you.”
So I went off, as he told me, into the field called Ardath,{i} and there I sat among the flowers and ate of the plants of the field, and the food they gave me satisfied me.
After seven days, as I lay on the grass, my heart was troubled again as before.
My mouth was opened, and I began to speak before the Most High:
“Lord, you showed yourself to our ancestors in the wilderness, in a place untrodden and unfruitful, when they were coming out of Egypt; and you declared,
‘Hear me, Israel; and you, offspring of Jacob, attend to my words.
For see, I am sowing my law in you, and it shall bring forth fruit in you, and you shall be glorified in it for ever.’
But our ancestors received the law and did not keep it, nor observe the statutes; yet the fruit of the law did not perish, nor could it, for it was yours.{j}
Those who received it perished, because they did not guard what had been sown in them.
Now this is the usual course: when the ground receives seed, or the sea a ship, or any vessel food or drink, and that into which the seed was sown or the thing put is destroyed,
then what was sown or put in, or what was received, is destroyed along with it; the things received no longer remain with us. But with us it has not been so.
For we who received the law have sinned and perished, and our heart also which received it;
but the law has not perished; it remains in its glory.”{k}
While these things were in my heart, I glanced about, and there to my right was a woman, lamenting and crying aloud, grieving deeply in her soul; her garments were rent, and ashes lay on her head.
So I put aside the thoughts with which I was occupied, turned to her,
and said, “Why are you weeping? Why are you grieved in soul?”
She said to me, “Let me be, my lord, so that I may bewail myself and add to my grief, for I am deeply embittered in spirit and brought very low.”
I said to her, “What has befallen you? Tell me.”
She said to me, “I, your servant, was barren and had no child, though I had a husband thirty years.
Hour after hour, day after day, all through those thirty years, I entreated the Most High by night and by day.

And after thirty years God heard your handmaid, looked upon my lowliness, considered my distress, and gave me a son. I rejoiced greatly over him, I and my husband and all my fellow townspeople, and we gave great honor to the Mighty One.
I brought him up with much toil.
And when he had grown and the time came for him to take a wife, I prepared a feast day.

notes.text: The oriental versions reportedly add, “confusion of nations, and disquiet of rulers.”
Compare 13:23. The Latin here reads “the faith in which you have believed,” addressing the readers directly.
Latin miserebuntur, “will be pitiable” or “will be wretched.”
In the Clementine Latin the words “He replied” stand at the end of verse 16; they are placed at the head of the answer.
The meaning of the last sentence is uncertain.

Latin “When I was preparing for them, for those who now are, before the world was made in which they would dwell, no one contradicted me.” The rendering combines the end of verse 18 with the start of verse 19, following the sense of the oriental versions as reported.
The words “and saw that it was lost; I saw my earth” are supplied from the oriental versions, as reported, where the Latin reads only “and behold, it was in peril.”
Compare Isaiah 65:8. Latin de tribu multa, “from a great tribe”; the rendering “forest” follows the oriental versions as reported.
The name Ardath is of unknown meaning and location; the oriental versions reportedly read Arpad, Araat, or similar forms.

verses.text: “But when my son went into his bridal chamber, he fell down and died.
Then we all overturned the lamps,{a} and all my townspeople rose up to console me; and I kept still until the evening of the next day.
When they had all left off consoling me, so that I might be quiet, I got up by night and fled, and came, as you see, to this field.
And I mean never to go back into the city, but to stay here, neither eating nor drinking, but mourning and fasting without a break until I die.”
Then I left the reflections in which I had been engaged, and answered her in anger:
“You most foolish of women, do you not see our grief, and what has happened to us?
For Zion, the mother of us all, is in deep sorrow and great humiliation, and mourns most bitterly.
And now, when we all mourn and are sad because we are all in sorrow, are you grieving over one son?
Ask the earth, and she will tell you that it is she who ought to mourn the fall of so many who have sprung up on her.
From her all have been born from the beginning, and others will come; and look, nearly all go to perdition, and their multitude is brought to destruction.
Who then ought to mourn more, she who has lost so great a multitude, or you, who are grieving for one?
But if you say to me, ‘My lament is not like the earth’s, for I have lost the fruit of my womb, which I bore in grief and brought forth in pain;
but with the earth it is the way of the earth: the multitude now in her has gone as it came’—then I say to you:
just as you gave birth with travail, so the earth from the beginning has given her fruit, humankind, to him who made her.
Now therefore keep your grief to yourself, and bear bravely the misfortunes that have befallen you.
For if you own God’s decree as just, in due season you will have your son back,{b} and among women you will win praise.
So go into the city to your husband.”
She said to me,{c} “I will not do it. I will not go into the city; I will die here.”
So I spoke to her once more, and said:
“Do not say such a thing, but let yourself be persuaded; for how many are the misfortunes of Zion! Take comfort because of the sorrow of Jerusalem.
For you see that our holy place has been laid waste, our altar thrown down, our temple destroyed;

our harp is brought low, our hymn silenced, our rejoicing ended; the light of our lampstand is put out, the ark of our covenant plundered, our holy things defiled, and the name by which we are called all but profaned; our children have suffered insult, our priests have been burned, our Levites have gone into captivity, our virgins have been defiled and our wives ravished, our righteous men carried off, our little ones lost, our young men enslaved, and our strong men made weak.
And greatest of all, the seal of Zion: she has been unsealed{d} from her glory and given over into the hands of those who hate us.
So shake off your great sadness and lay aside the throng of your sorrows, so that the Mighty One may be reconciled to you again, and the Most High may give you rest, a respite from your troubles.”
While I was speaking to her, all at once her face shone exceedingly, and her countenance flashed like lightning, so that I was greatly afraid to go near her, and wondered what this might be.
Suddenly she let out a loud cry, full of fear, so that the earth shook at the sound. I looked,
and the woman was no longer visible to me, but there was a city being built,{e} and a place showed itself with massive foundations. I was afraid and cried aloud:
“Where is Uriel the angel, who came to me at the first? It is he who has made me fall into this great bewilderment; my end has become corruption, and my prayer a reproach.”
While I was saying this, he came to me and looked at me.
There I lay like a dead man, bereft of understanding. He took hold of my right hand, gave me strength, set me on my feet, and said to me,
“What is wrong with you? Why are your understanding and the thoughts of your heart troubled? Why are you disturbed?”
I said, “Because you forsook me! I did as you told me, and went out into the field, and look, I have seen, and still see, what I cannot describe.”
He told me, “Stand up like a man, and I will counsel you.”
I said, “Speak to me, my lord; do not forsake me, lest I die before my time.{f}
Things unknown to me I have beheld, and things beyond my knowing I am hearing.
Can it be that my senses are cheated, and my soul is in a dream?
Now, then, I entreat you to explain to your servant this bewildering vision.”
He replied, “Hear me, and I will teach you, and tell you about the things you fear; for the Most High has revealed many secrets to you.
He has seen your upright way: that you have grieved without ceasing for your people, and mourned greatly over Zion.
This, then, is the meaning of the vision that appeared to you a little while ago.
You saw a woman mourning, and you began to console her;
but now you no longer see the form of a woman; instead a city being built has appeared to you.
And as for her telling you of the misfortune of her son, this is the explanation:
This woman whom you saw is Zion, whom you now see as a city built.{g}
And as for her telling you that she was barren thirty years, it is because for three thousand years{h} no offering had yet been offered in her.
Then, after three thousand years, Solomon built the city and offered offerings; that was when the barren woman bore a son.
Her words that she reared him with toil signify the time of dwelling in Jerusalem.
And as for her telling you, ‘My son died when he entered his bridal chamber, and misfortune befell him,’ that was the ruin which came upon Jerusalem.
And look, you have seen her likeness, how she mourned her son, and you began to console her for what had befallen her. These were the things to be disclosed to you.
For now the Most High, seeing that you were grieved to your very soul and suffered with all your heart on her account, has shown you the brilliance of her glory and the loveliness of her beauty.
That is why I told you to stay in the field where no house had been built;
I was aware that the Most High meant to begin revealing these things to you.
That was why I bade you come to open ground, where no building had a foundation.
for no work of human building could endure in the place where the city of the Most High was to be shown.
Do not fear, then, and let no terror seize your heart; enter, and behold how splendid and how vast the edifice is, so far as your eyes have power to see it;
and afterward you will hear as much as your ears can take in.
For you are blessed beyond many, and are called before the Most High as only a few are.
But tomorrow night you are to remain here,
and the Most High will show you those visions in dreams{i} of what the Most High will do to those who dwell on the earth in the last days.” So I slept that night and the next, as he had told me.{j}

notes.text: Latin evertimus omnes lumina, “we all overturned the lamps,” a sign of mourning; the oriental versions reportedly read “put out the lamps.”
Latin “you will receive his counsel in time”; the rendering follows the sense of the oriental versions as reported.
In the Clementine Latin the words “She said to me” stand at the end of verse 17; they are placed at the head of her reply.
Latin resignata, “unsealed,” that is, her seal is broken and her glory taken away.
The heavenly Jerusalem (compare 7:26; 8:52; 13:36).
Latin ut non frustra moriar, “lest I die in vain.”
The Latin of this verse is broken; the rendering follows the sense.

Latin triginta, “thirty”; the oriental versions reportedly read “three thousand years,” referring to the years from creation to Solomon’s temple, and the rendering follows that reading in verses 45–46 in place of the Latin “thirty.”
Latin visiones supremorum, “visions of the highest (or last) things”; the words “in dreams” follow the oriental versions as reported.
In the Clementine Latin the last sentence is a separate verse (10:60), so that the chapter has 60 verses; the numbering of most English versions is followed here.

verses.text: On the second night{a} I had a dream: there was an eagle rising up from the sea, with twelve feathered wings and three heads.{b}
I looked: over all the land it stretched out its wings, every wind of the sky breathed on it, and the clouds{c} massed together around it.
I watched, and from its wings there grew opposing wings,{d} and these became little, puny wings.
Its heads lay quiet; the one in the middle was bigger than its fellows, yet it also lay quiet along with them.
I watched, and the eagle flew with its wings and reigned over the earth and over those who dwell in it.
I saw that everything under heaven was subject to it, and no one spoke against it, not one creature on the earth.
I watched, and the eagle rose up on its talons and gave a cry to its wings, saying,
“Do not all keep watch at once; let each sleep in its own place, and keep watch in turn;
but let the heads be kept for the last.”
I looked, and the cry came not out of its heads, but out of the midst of its body.
Then I numbered its opposing wings: eight in all.
I watched, and on the right side one wing arose and reigned over all the earth.
And while it was reigning, its end came, and it disappeared, so that its place was not seen. The next arose and reigned, and it held sway a long time.
And while it was reigning, its end came too, so that it vanished like the first.
Then a voice sounded, saying to it,
“Hear me, you who have held the earth all this time; I announce this to you before you begin to vanish:
after you, no one will hold sway as long as you, or even half as long.”{e}
Then the third raised itself up and held the rule like those before, and it also disappeared.
And so it befell all the wings one after another, to bear rule and then to vanish from sight.
I watched, and in due course the wings that followed were raised up on the right side,{f} that they also might hold the rule; and some of them held it, but at once disappeared;
and some of them were raised up, but did not hold the rule.
After this I looked: gone were the twelve wings, gone two of the small wings,
and nothing was left on the eagle’s body except the two heads that were at rest and six little wings.
I watched, and two of the six little wings separated themselves and remained under the head on the right side; but four remained in their place.
I watched, and these underwings planned to raise themselves up and hold the rule.
I watched, and one was raised up, but at once vanished;
and the second vanished even more swiftly than the first.
I watched, and the two that remained were plotting between themselves to reign as well.
And while they were plotting, one of the heads that were at rest, the one in the middle, woke up; for it was greater than the other two heads.
And I perceived that it joined the pair of heads to itself,
and that head, together with its companions, swung round and swallowed up the two underwings that were scheming for the kingdom.
This head struck terror into the whole earth, and lorded it over earth’s dwellers with great oppression, and held power over the world more than all the wings that had been.
After this I looked, and suddenly the middle head too disappeared, just as the wings had.
But two heads remained, and they also reigned in like manner over the earth and those who dwell in it.
I looked, and the head on the right side devoured the one on the left.
Then I heard a voice telling me, “Look in front of you, and consider what you see.”
I looked, and there came a lion-like creature, stirred up out of the woods and roaring; and I heard it speak with a man’s voice to the eagle, addressing it thus:
“Hear, for I have words for you. Thus says the Most High:
Are you not the survivor of the four beasts{g} whom I set to rule in my world, that through them the close of their times might arrive?

You, the fourth, coming last, overcame every beast that was before you, and ruled the world with great terror, and the whole globe with cruel oppression; for long ages you have inhabited the earth by fraud.
You have judged the earth, but not with truth;
for you have afflicted the meek and injured the peaceable; you have loved liars, destroyed the dwellings of the fruitful, and torn down the walls of those who did you no harm.
Your insolence has gone up to the Most High, and your pride to the Mighty One.
The Most High has looked upon his{h} times, and see, they are ended, and his ages are complete.
Therefore vanish, eagle—you, your dreadful wings, your wicked small wings, your spiteful heads, your evil claws, and all your empty body—
so that the whole earth may be refreshed and relieved, set free from your violence, and may hope for the judgment and mercy of him who made it.”

notes.text: The fifth vision (11:1–12:51) is the vision of the eagle. The words “On the second night” are not in the Clementine Latin, which begins “And I saw a dream”; they are reportedly found in other witnesses.

The eagle stands for the Roman Empire (12:11), identified with the fourth kingdom of Daniel 7:7, 23. The wings and heads are generally understood as Roman emperors; the three heads are often taken to be Vespasian, Titus, and Domitian (AD 69–96), but the identifications are disputed.
Latin “and they were gathered together”; the words “the clouds … about it” are supplied from the oriental versions, as reported.
Latin contrariae pennae, “opposing wings,” perhaps rival claimants or lesser rulers.
Often taken to refer to Augustus, who ruled the empire for over forty years (27 BC–AD 14).
Latin “from the right side”; the text of verses 20–21 is uncertain.
The four beasts of Daniel 7:3–7.

Latin superba tempora, “the proud times”; the rendering follows the sense of the oriental versions as reported, “his (that is, God’s) times.” The Latin scelera ejus, “its crimes,” is likewise rendered from the oriental versions, as reported.

verses.text: While the lion was speaking these words to the eagle, I looked,
and there was the head that had remained; and the four wings{a} that had gone over to it had disappeared, though they had been raised up to reign; and their reign was feeble and full of tumult.

I looked, and they too had vanished, and the whole body of the eagle was set on fire, and the earth was struck with great dread. Then out of the tumult and the frenzy of my mind, and out of my great fear, I woke, and said to my spirit,
“See, you have brought this upon me, because you search out the ways of the Most High.
Look, my mind is worn out still, my spirit is utterly weak, and hardly any strength remains in me, so greatly was I terrified this night.
So now I will pray to the Most High to strengthen me to the end.”
I said, “Lord and Master, if I have found favor in your sight, and if I am counted righteous before you above many, and if my supplication has truly come up before your face,
strengthen me, and show your servant the interpretation and the clear meaning of this fearful vision, so that you may fully console my soul.
For you have judged me worthy to be shown the last of the times.”
He told me,{b} “This is the interpretation of this vision of yours:
The eagle that you saw rising from the sea is the kingdom which appeared in a vision to your brother Daniel.{c}
But it was not interpreted to him as I now interpret it to you.
Look, the days are coming when a kingdom will rise on the earth, and it will be more dreadful than all the kingdoms that were before it.
Twelve kings will reign in it, one after another.
But the second to begin reigning will hold sway for a longer time than any of the twelve.
This is the meaning of the twelve wings you saw.
As for the voice you heard speaking, not issuing from its heads but from the midst of its body,
this is the meaning: after the time of that kingdom{d} no small strife will arise, and it will be in danger of falling; yet it will not fall then, but will be restored to its former state.
As for your seeing eight underwings clinging to its wings,
this is the meaning: eight kings will arise in it, whose times will be brief and their years swift; two of them will perish.
As the middle of its time draws near, four will be kept until the time when its end begins to approach; but two will be kept for the end.
As for your seeing three heads at rest,
this is the meaning: in its last days the Most High will raise up three kings,{e} and they will renew many things in it, and will rule over the earth
and its dwellers with more oppression than all who were before them. That is why they are called the heads of the eagle;
for it is they who will sum up its godlessness, and who will bring its last days to completion.
As for your seeing the greater head disappear, this is its meaning: one of them will die on his bed, yet in torments.{f}
As for the two who remain, the sword will devour them.
For the sword of the one will devour his companion; but he too will fall by the sword in the last days.{g}
As for your seeing two underwings passing over to the head on the right side,
this is the meaning: these are the ones whom the Most High has kept for its end; this is the feeble reign, full of turmoil, as you saw.
As for the lion that you saw roused out of the forest, roaring and speaking to the eagle and reproving it for its wrongdoing in all the words you heard,

this is the Anointed One,{h} reserved by the Most High for the close of the days, sprung from David’s line, who will come and address them. He will rebuke them for their godlessness and their wicked deeds, and will lay before them their acts of contempt.{i}
For first he will set them alive in judgment, and when he has reproved them, then he will destroy them.
Yet my people who are left, the ones saved within my borders, he will set free with compassion, and gladden them until the end arrives, the day of judgment, of which I told you at the outset.
This is the dream that you saw, and this is its interpretation.
And you alone have been worthy to learn this secret of the Most High.
So write all these things that you have seen in a book, and put it in a hidden place;
and teach them to the wise among your people, whose hearts you know are able to grasp and keep these secrets.
But as for you, wait here seven more days, so that whatever it pleases the Most High to show you may be shown to you.” Then he left me.{j}
When all the people heard that seven days had passed and I had not gone back to the city, they all gathered, from the least to the greatest, and came to me and said to me,
“How have we sinned against you, and what wrong have we done you, that you have forsaken us and sit in this place?
For of all the peoples you alone are left to us, like a cluster from the vintage, like a lamp in a dark place, like a haven and a ship saved from the storm.
Are not the evils that have befallen us enough?
If you forsake us, how much better it would have been for us if we too had been burned up in the burning of Zion!
We are not better than the ones who perished there.” Then they wailed aloud.
“Take courage, Israel; and do not be sad, house of Jacob.
For you are remembered before the Most High, and the Mighty One has not forgotten you in your trial.{k}
I have not forsaken you, nor gone away from you; but I came to this place to pray over the desolation of Zion, and to seek mercy for the low estate of your sanctuary.
Now go, each of you, to your house, and I will come to you after these days.”
So the people went into the city, as I told them.
But I sat in the field seven days, as he had commanded me; and in those days I ate only the flowers of the field, and my food was of plants.

notes.text: Latin “the four wings”; perhaps the four little wings of 11:24.
In the Latin, “And he said to me” stands at the end of verse 9; it is placed at the head of the reply.
Daniel 7:7–8, 23–27. Here the fourth kingdom of Daniel, originally the Greek empire, is reinterpreted as Rome.
Usually taken as the civil wars of AD 68–69 after the death of Nero, when the empire nearly fell and was restored under Vespasian.
Latin regna, “kingdoms”; the rendering follows the sense of the oriental versions, as reported.
Often taken as Vespasian, who died a natural death in AD 79.

The Latin of verse 28 is confused. It is commonly taken to refer to Domitian, who was popularly (and probably wrongly) believed to have killed his brother Titus, and who was himself assassinated in AD 96.

“Anointed One” is Messiah (Hebrew) or Christ (Greek). The Latin reads ventus, “wind,” evidently a corruption; the rendering follows the oriental versions as reported, which also supply the words “until the end of days … and speak to them.”
Latin discerptiones, “acts of contempt” or “insults”; the meaning is uncertain.
In the Latin, “Then he left me” stands at the beginning of verse 40.
Latin in tentatione, “in temptation” or “in trial.”

verses.text: After seven days I dreamed a dream by night.{a}
There was a wind rising out of the sea, which stirred up all its waves.

As I watched, that wind brought up out of the depths of the sea something like the figure of a man;{b} and this man flew with the clouds of heaven.{c} Wherever he turned his face to look, everything seen beneath him trembled;
and wherever the voice went forth from his mouth, all who heard his voice melted away, as wax melts{d} when it feels the fire.
After this I looked, and a multitude of people past numbering was being gathered from the four winds of heaven to make war on the man who had come up out of the sea.
I watched, and he carved out for himself a great mountain and flew up on it.
I sought to see the region or place from which the mountain had been carved, and could not.
After this I looked, and all who had gathered against him to fight him were seized with great fear, yet they dared to fight.
And when he saw the onrush of the multitude as it came, he did not lift his hand, nor hold a spear{e} or any weapon of war; but I saw only

but only how he poured out of his mouth what looked like a torrent of fire, and out of his lips a fiery blast, and out of his tongue he hurled sparks and tempests; and all of these mingled together, the torrent of fire, the fiery blast, and the mighty tempest,

and fell upon the onrushing multitude prepared for battle, and burned them all up, so that suddenly nothing was to be seen of that countless multitude but only dust of ashes and the smell of smoke. I saw it and was astounded.
After this I saw that man coming down from the mountain and calling to himself another multitude, a peaceable one.

Then the forms of many people came to him, some of them glad and some sorrowful; some were in bonds, and some were bringing others as offerings.{f} Then I fell sick from the greatness of my fear; I woke, and said,
“From the beginning you have shown your servant these wonders, and have judged me worthy to have my supplication received;
now show me also the interpretation of this dream.
For as I reckon in my understanding, woe to those who are left in those days, and much more woe to those who are not left!
For those who are not left will be in sorrow,
since they understand what is laid up for the last days, but will not attain it.{g} But woe also to those who are left,
for this very reason, that they will see great perils and much distress, as these dreams show.
Yet it is better to come into these things, though in peril, than to pass away like a cloud from the world and not see what will happen at the last.”
He replied,{h} “I will tell you the interpretation of the vision, and I will also lay open to you the things of which you have spoken.
Concerning your words about the ones who are left, here is the meaning:
the one who causes the danger in that season will keep safe the ones who meet with danger, if they have works and faith toward the Almighty.{i}
Know, then, that those who are left are more blessed than those who have died.
Here is what the vision signifies: you beheld a man ascending out of the sea’s heart;
this is he whom the Most High is keeping for many ages, who will himself set free his creation; and he will order the lot of those who are left.
As for your seeing wind and fire and storm come out of his mouth,
and that he held no spear or weapon of war, yet his onrush destroyed the multitude that came to make war on him, this is the meaning:
the days are coming when the Most High will begin to deliver those who are on the earth.
And bewilderment of mind{j} will come upon the dwellers on earth.
They will plot to make war on one another, city against city, place against place, nation against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
When these things come to pass, and the signs occur which I showed you before, then my son{k} will be revealed, whom you saw as a man coming up from the sea.
And when all the nations hear his voice, each of them will leave behind, in its own land, the warfare that they wage against one another;
and a countless multitude will be gathered together, as you saw, wishing to come and make war on him.
But he will stand on the summit of Mount Zion.
And Zion will come and be shown to all, prepared and built, as you saw the mountain carved out without hands.{l}
And he, my son, will reprove the nations that have come for their godlessness—this was signified by the storm{m}—

and will set before them their evil thoughts and the torments with which they will be tormented, which were signified by the flame; and he will destroy them without labor by the law, which was signified by the fire.
You beheld him summon another throng to himself, a peaceable one:

these are the ten tribes which were led away captive from their own land in the days of King Hoshea,{n} whom Shalmaneser{o} the king of the Assyrians led captive; he carried them across the River, and they were taken into another land.
But they formed this plan among themselves, to leave the multitude of the nations and go to a more distant region, where the human race had never dwelt,
that there at least they might keep their statutes, which they had not kept in their own land.
And they went in by the narrow passages of the Euphrates River.
For the Most High then did signs for them, and stopped the channels of the river until they had crossed over.
The road through that country was long, a march of eighteen months; and the region bears the name Arzareth.{p}
There they have dwelt until the last time; and now, when they are about to come again,
the Most High will once more hold back the river’s channels to let them pass over. This is why the throng you beheld was at peace.
But those of your people who are left are those who are found within my holy border.{q}
So when he destroys the multitude of the nations that are gathered together, he will protect the people who remain.
And then he will show them very many wonders.”
I said, “Lord and Master, show me this: why did I see the man coming up from the heart of the sea?” He told me,
“Just as no one can search out or know what is in the depths of the sea, so no one on earth can see my son, or those who are with him, except in the time of his day.{r}
This is the interpretation of the dream that you saw; and on account of it you alone have been enlightened here.
For you have forsaken your own ways, and have given yourself to mine, and have searched out my law.
You have ordered your life in wisdom, and have called understanding your mother.
That is why I have shown you this; for there is a reward with the Most High. After three more days I will tell you other things, and set before you weighty and wonderful matters.”
So I went out to the field, glorifying and praising the Most High greatly for the marvels he works at their appointed times,
and because he rules the seasons and all that is brought about in them. Three days I remained there.

notes.text: The sixth vision (13:1–58), the man from the sea.
The Latin lacks the words “that wind … the figure of a man”; they are supplied from the oriental versions, as reported, since a line has evidently dropped out of the Latin.

Latin convalescebat cum millibus caeli, “grew strong with the thousands of heaven,” evidently a corruption; the rendering follows the oriental versions as reported. Compare Daniel 7:13, “one like a son of man, coming with the clouds of heaven.”
Latin “as the earth is at rest when it feels fire,” evidently corrupt; the rendering follows the oriental versions as reported. Compare Psalm 97:5; Micah 1:4.
Latin framea, a Germanic spear; here simply “spear.”
The Latin of this verse is obscure; compare Isaiah 66:20, where the nations bring the scattered Israelites as an offering.
The Latin of verses 17–18 is confused; the rendering follows the sense of the oriental versions, as reported.
In the Latin, “And he answered me and said” stands at the end of verse 20.
Latin Fortissimum, “the Mightiest One.” The Latin of this verse is obscure.
Latin excessus mentis, “frenzy” or “ecstasy” of mind.

The Latin filius meus, “my son,” here and in verses 37 and 52 and in 14:9, reportedly corresponds to “my servant” in some oriental versions, and may render Greek pais, which can mean either “son” or “servant.” Compare 7:28–29.
Compare Daniel 2:34, 45, the stone cut out without hands.
Latin of verses 37–38 is confused; the rendering follows the sense of the oriental versions, as reported, which explain the storm, the flame, and the fire of verses 10–11.
Hoshea (“salvation”), last king of the northern kingdom of Israel (2 Kings 17:1–6), about 732–722 BC.
Shalmaneser V, king of Assyria, 727–722 BC; the name means “(the god) Shulmanu is foremost.”
Arzareth (Latin Arsareth) is probably a corruption of Hebrew erets aheret, “another land,” from Deuteronomy 29:28, the verse that later rabbinic tradition applied to the lost ten tribes.
Latin “within my border”; the word “holy” is supplied from the oriental versions, as reported.
Latin nisi in tempore diei, “except in the time of the day”; the oriental versions reportedly read “of his day.”

verses.text: On the third day, as I was sitting under an oak,{a}
when out of a bush facing me a voice spoke: “Ezra, Ezra!” I answered, “Here I am, Lord,” and stood up on my feet. He told me,
“I revealed myself openly in the bush and spoke to Moses, when my people were slaves in Egypt;
and I sent him and led my people out of Egypt, and brought him up on Mount Sinai, and kept him with me many days.
I told him many wondrous things, and showed him the secrets of the times and the end;{b} and I commanded him, saying,
‘These words you shall make public, and these you shall keep hidden.’
And now I say to you:
lay up in your heart the signs that I have shown you, the dreams that you have seen, and the interpretations that you have heard;
for you will be taken up from among human beings, and from then on you will dwell with my son{c} and with those who are like you, until the times are ended.
For the world has lost its youth, and the times are drawing near to old age.
For the world{d} is split into twelve portions; nine portions are gone already, and half of the tenth;
and there remain of it two parts, besides half of the tenth part.{e}
Now therefore set your house in order, warn your people, comfort the lowly among them, and renounce now the life of corruption.
Put away from you mortal thoughts, cast off from you the burdens of humankind, strip off now your feeble nature, set aside the thoughts that trouble you most, and hasten to depart from these times.
For evils worse than those you have now seen happen will be done hereafter.
For the feebler the world grows with age, so much the more will evils abound upon its dwellers.
Truth will withdraw farther off, and falsehood draw near; for the eagle{f} you saw in the vision is already hastening to come.”
Then I replied, “Let me speak before you, Lord.
See, I will go, as you have commanded me, and I will warn the people who are now living; but who will warn those born hereafter?
For the world lies in darkness, and its dwellers are without light.
For your law has been burned,{g} and so no one knows the things that have been done by you, or the works that are to begin.

But if I have found favor before you, send the Holy Spirit into me, and I will set down everything done in the world since its beginning, all that stood written in your law, that people may find the path, and that any who desire life in the last days may live.”
He replied, “Go, gather the people, and tell them not to seek you for forty days.
But prepare for yourself many writing tablets,{h} and take with you Sarea, Dabria, Selemia, Ethanus, and Asiel,{i} these five, because they are trained to write swiftly;
Then come back here; I will kindle a lamp of understanding in your heart, and it will not go out until the writing you begin is complete.
When the work is done, part of it you are to publish, and part you are to hand on secretly to the wise. At this hour tomorrow the writing will begin.”
So I went, as he had commanded me, and gathered all the people, and said,
“Hear these words, Israel.
At the first our ancestors dwelt as strangers in Egypt, and they were set free from there,
and received the law of life, which they did not keep, and which you also have transgressed after them.
Afterward a land was granted to you as an inheritance in the land of Zion; yet you and your forebears committed iniquity and failed to walk in the ways the Most High laid down for you.
And because he is a righteous judge, in due time he took from you what he had given.
And now you are here, and your kindred are farther inland than you.{j}
If, then, you will rule over your understanding and discipline your heart, you will be kept alive, and after death you will obtain mercy.
For after death the judgment will come, when we live once more; and then the names of the righteous will become manifest, and the deeds of the godless will be disclosed.
But let no one come to me now, nor seek me for forty days.”
So I took the five men, as he commanded me, and we went out into the field and stayed there.
Next day a voice summoned me: “Ezra, open your mouth, and drink the draught I offer you.”
So I opened my mouth, and a full cup was held out to me; it was full of something like water, but its color was like fire.
I received it and drank; and as soon as I had drunk, understanding welled up from my heart, wisdom grew within my breast, and my spirit held fast its memory;{k}
and my mouth was opened, and was not closed again.
The Most High gave understanding to the five men, and they wrote what was spoken, in turn, in characters which they did not know.{l} They sat forty days;
they ate their bread by night;{m} but as for me, I spoke by day, and by night I was not silent.
So in forty days ninety-four{n} books were written.
At the end of the forty days the Most High said to me, “The twenty-four books{o} you wrote first, publish openly, for the worthy and unworthy alike to read;
the seventy written afterward, however, you are to keep and hand on to the wise of your people.
For in them is the spring of understanding, the fountain of wisdom, and the river of knowledge.”
And I did so.{p}

notes.text: The seventh vision (14:1–48), Ezra and the restoration of the scriptures. The oak recalls Abraham at Mamre (Genesis 18:1).
Compare 2 Baruch 59:4–11, where Moses is likewise shown the secrets of the end on Sinai.
See the note on 13:32.
Latin saeculum. The division of world history into twelve parts is reportedly lacking or different in some oriental versions.

The Latin of verses 11–12 is reportedly confused in the manuscripts (“ten and a half parts have passed”); the rendering follows the sense of the oriental versions as reported, which agree that the greater part of the world’s time is past.
Latin “the vision which you saw”; the word “eagle” follows the oriental versions, as reported, referring to the eagle vision of chapters 11–12.

Referring to the destruction of the temple and its scrolls by the Babylonians in 587 BC (compare 4:23). The story that Ezra restored the scriptures by inspiration is reflected in some early Christian writers.
Latin buxos, “boxwood tablets,” wooden tablets coated with wax for writing.

The five scribes’ names are reportedly uncertain and appear differently in the versions; the Latin reads Saream, Dabriam, Selemiam, Echanum, and Asiel. Selemia is probably Shelemiah, “Yahweh has repaid”; Asiel probably means “God has made”; the others are of uncertain meaning.
Latin introrsum vestrum, “within you” or “farther in,” probably referring to the ten tribes beyond the Euphrates (13:40–45).
Latin “my spirit was kept in memory.”

Latin excessiones noctis, “the outpourings of the night,” evidently a corruption; the rendering follows the oriental versions as reported. The “characters they did not know” are commonly taken to be the square Aramaic script, which in Jewish tradition Ezra introduced in place of the older Hebrew script.
The Latin has “they ate bread at night” at the beginning of the verse; the words “They sat forty days” at the end of verse 42 are supplied from the oriental versions, as reported.
Latin ducenti quattuor, “two hundred and four”; other Latin witnesses and the oriental versions reportedly read “ninety-four.” The seventy hidden books are esoteric writings such as this one.

The twenty-four books are the Hebrew scriptures as counted in Jewish tradition (the Torah, the Prophets, and the Writings, with the Twelve counted as one book, and Ezra–Nehemiah and Chronicles each as one). The number “twenty-four” is supplied from the oriental versions, as reported; the Latin reads “the first books.”

In the Clementine Latin these words end verse 47, and the book of 4 Ezra ends here. The oriental versions reportedly continue: “in the seventh year of the sixth week, five thousand years and three months and twelve days after creation. At that time Ezra was caught up and taken to the place of those who are like him, after he had written all these things; and he was called the Scribe of the knowledge of the Most High for ever and ever.” This is the “taking up” referred to in 8:20 and 14:9. Most English versions number the words “And I did so” as verse 48.

verses.text: “See, speak in the hearing of my people the words of prophecy which I will put in your mouth,{a} says the Lord;
and have them written on paper,{b} for they are trustworthy and true.
Do not fear the plots against you, and do not let the unbelief of those who speak against you trouble you.
For every unbeliever will die in his unbelief.”
“Look, I am bringing evils upon the whole world, says the Lord: sword and famine, death and ruin;
because iniquity has utterly defiled the whole earth, and their harmful deeds have reached their full measure.
Therefore, says the Lord,

I will no longer keep silent about their godlessness, which they commit so impiously, nor will I put up with their wicked practices. Look, innocent and righteous blood cries out to me, and the souls of the righteous cry out without ceasing.
I will surely avenge them, says the Lord, and will require from them all the innocent blood shed among them.
See, my people are led like a flock to the slaughter. I will no longer let them live in the land of Egypt,
but I will bring them out with a mighty hand and an uplifted arm, and will strike Egypt with plagues as before, and will destroy all its land.
Egypt will mourn, and its foundations will be struck with the blow and the chastisement that God will bring upon it.
Those who till the soil will mourn, because their seed will fail through blight and hail and a fearful star.{c}
Woe to the world and its dwellers!
For the sword and their ruin are drawing near; nation will rise up against nation in battle, with swords in their hands.
For there will be unrest among people; growing strong against one another, they will pay no heed to their king, and their princes will reckon their deeds by their own might.{d}
A person will long to go into a city, and will not be able to.
For because of their pride the cities will be in turmoil, the houses will be destroyed, and people will be afraid.
No one will have pity on a neighbor, but they will make an assault on their houses with the sword and plunder their goods, because of hunger for bread and great distress.

“Look, says God, I am calling together all the kings of the earth to revere me, those from the rising sun and from the south, from the east and from Lebanon,{e} to turn upon one another and repay what has been done to them.
As they are doing to my chosen ones to this day, so I will do, and will repay into their laps. This is what the Lord God says:
My right hand will show no mercy to sinners, nor will my sword rest from any who pour out guiltless blood upon the earth.”
And fire went forth from his wrath and consumed the foundations of the earth, and the sinners like burning straw.
“Woe to those who sin and do not keep my commandments, says the Lord;
I will not spare them. Depart, you rebellious children,{f} and do not defile my sanctuary.”
The Lord is aware of everyone who offends against him; that is why he has given them up to death and to slaughter.
For evils have already come upon the whole earth, and you will remain in them; for God will not deliver you, because you have sinned against him.
See, a fearful sight, and its appearance from the east!
The nations of the dragons of Arabia{g} will come out with many chariots, and their multitude will be borne like the wind across the earth, so that all who hear them will fear and tremble.

The Carmonians,{h} raging in wrath, will go forth like wild boars of the forest, and come with great power, and join battle with them, and lay waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians with their teeth.{i}
And after this the dragons, remembering their origin, will gain the upper hand; and they will turn, conspiring together in great power, to pursue them.
And these will be thrown into confusion and fall silent before their power, and will turn their feet in flight.
And from the land of the Assyrians one lying in ambush will besiege them and destroy one of them; and there will be fear and trembling in their army, and strife among their kings.
See, clouds from the east, and from the north to the south! Their appearance is very dreadful, full of wrath and storm.
They will dash against one another, and will pour out a heavy storm{j} upon the earth, their own storm; and there will be blood from the sword as high as a horse’s belly,{k}
and as high as a man’s thigh and a camel’s hock.{l} Fear and much trembling will be upon the earth;
those who see that wrath will shudder, and trembling will seize them. After this, great storm clouds will be stirred up
from the south and the north, and another part from the west.
But the winds from the east will prevail, and will shut in the cloud which he raised up in wrath; and the storm that was to bring destruction by the east wind and the west will be driven back.{m}

Then great and mighty clouds, full of wrath, will be lifted up, and the storm, to make the whole earth and its dwellers afraid; and they will pour out a terrible storm over every high and lofty place,
fire and hail, swords on the wing, and torrents of water, until every field and every stream is brimming with an abundance of waters.
They will tear down cities and walls, mountains and hills, the trees of the forests and the grass of the meadows, and their grain.
They will go on steadily as far as Babylon,{n} and will destroy it.
They will come to it and surround it, and pour out the storm and all their wrath upon it; then dust and smoke will go up to heaven, and all who are around it will mourn for it.
And those who survive under it will serve those who have struck it with terror.
“And you, Asia,{o} who share in the hope of Babylon and in her glorious repute,

woe to you, wretched one, because you have made yourself like her; you have decked out your daughters in harlotry, to please and to glory in your lovers, who have always lusted to commit harlotry with you.
You have copied the hated city in all that she does and in all her schemes. Therefore, says God,
I will send evils upon you: widowhood, poverty, famine, sword, and pestilence, to lay waste your houses with violence and death, and the glory of your strength.{p}
Like a flower you will wither, when the burning heat rises that is sent upon you.
You will be weakened like a poor woman, beaten and wounded,{q} so that your mighty ones and your lovers cannot receive you.
Would I have been so jealous against you, says the Lord,
if you had not always killed my chosen ones, exulting and clapping your hands and talking over their death when you were drunk?
Beautify your face!
The wages of your harlotry are in your lap; therefore you will receive your recompense.
What you do to my chosen, says the Lord, God will do in turn to you, giving you over to evil.
Your children will die of hunger, and you will fall by the sword; your cities will be crushed, and all your people in the open country will fall by the sword.{r}
Those in the mountains will perish of hunger, and they will eat their own flesh and drink their own blood, for hunger of bread and thirst for water.
You will come, unhappy one, across the seas, and again you will meet with evils.
And as they pass by, they will dash against the city that was slain,{s} and will destroy some portion of your land, and wipe out part of your glory, as they return once more from Babylon laid waste.
You will be torn down by them like stubble, and they will be fire to you.
They will devour you and your cities, your land and your mountains; they will burn up with fire all your forests and your fruitful trees.
They will carry your children away captive, take your wealth as plunder, and wipe out the glory of your face.”

notes.text: Chapters 15–16, known as 6 Ezra, are a Christian addition, reportedly from the 3rd century AD, perhaps written in the eastern Roman Empire during a time of persecution. A Greek fragment of 15:57–59 has reportedly been found in an Oxyrhynchus papyrus (P. Oxy. 1010), showing that this section was first written in Greek. These chapters are not in the oriental versions.
Latin charta, “papyrus” or “paper.”
Latin sidus, “star” or “constellation”; in these chapters the word seems to stand for a destructive storm, and from verse 35 on it is rendered “storm.”
The Latin of this verse is obscure.

“From the rising sun … the east”: Latin ab Oriente … ab Euro, the latter properly the southeast wind. Lebanon (“white,” from its snowy peaks) perhaps stands here for the north or west. The text may be corrupt.
Latin discedite filii a potestate, “depart, children, from the power,” obscure; perhaps “depart, you apostate children.”

Latin dracones Arabum, “dragons of the Arabians.” Some interpreters see an allusion to the armies of Odenathus and Zenobia of Palmyra in the AD 260s, who fought the Persians; the identification is uncertain.
Latin carmonii, probably the people of Carmania, a province of Persia on the north shore of the Persian Gulf; here perhaps the Persians under Shapur I (AD 240–270).

The words “with their teeth” are not in the Clementine Latin; they are reportedly found in another Latin manuscript tradition. Assyria here may stand for Syria, which was overrun by the Persians in the AD 250s.
See the note on verse 13.
Compare 1 Enoch 100:3 and Revelation 14:20.

Latin fimus hominis usque ad substramen cameli, “human dung up to the camel’s litter,” evidently corrupt; the rendering follows a common emendation, femur (“thigh”) for fimus (“dung”) and suffraginem (“hock”) for substramen.
The Latin of this verse is very obscure.
Babylon, as in Revelation 17–18, stands for Rome.
Asia here is the Roman province of Asia, in western Asia Minor (modern western Turkey); its chief cities included Ephesus, Smyrna, and Pergamum.
Latin “with violence and death, and the glory of your strength”; the text is obscure.
Latin castigata a mulieribus, “chastised by women,” probably a corruption for “wounded.”
A Greek fragment of verses 57–59 has reportedly been found among the Oxyrhynchus papyri (see the note on 15:1).
Latin civitatem occisam, “the slain city,” obscure; perhaps meaning Rome laid waste, or a corruption.

verses.text: Woe to you, Babylon and Asia! Woe to you, Egypt and Syria!{a}
Wrap yourselves in sackcloth and haircloth, beat your breasts for your children, and grieve; for your ruin is close at hand.
A sword has been sent against you; who is there to turn it back?
A fire has been sent among you; who is there to quench it?
Evils have been sent upon you; who is there to drive them away?
Can anyone drive off a hungry lion in the forest, or put out a fire in stubble once it has begun to blaze?
Can anyone turn back an arrow shot by a strong archer?
The Lord God sends the evils; who is there to drive them away?
Fire has gone out from his anger; who is there to quench it?
He will flash lightning, and who will not fear? He will thunder, and who will not shudder?
The Lord will threaten, and who will not be crushed to pieces before his face?
The earth and its foundations quake; the sea heaves up from the deep, and its waves and its fish are thrown into turmoil before the face of the Lord and the glory of his might.
For strong is his right hand that bends the bow; sharp are the arrows that he shoots, and once they begin to be sent to the ends of the earth, they will not miss.
See, the evils are sent forth, and will not turn back until they come upon the earth.
The fire is kindled, and will not be put out until it consumes the foundations of the earth.
As an arrow shot by a mighty archer does not come back, so the evils that are sent upon the earth will not turn back.
Woe is me, woe is me! Who will rescue me in those days?
The beginning of sorrows, and much groaning; the beginning of famine, and many deaths; the beginning of wars, and the powers will be afraid; the beginning of evils, and all will tremble!
What shall I do in these things, when the evils come?
Look: hunger and pestilence, affliction and distress have been dispatched as whips to bring correction;
yet for all these things they will not turn from their iniquities, nor ever keep the scourges in mind.
See, food will be so cheap on the earth that people will suppose peace is assured; and then evils will spring up on the earth: sword, famine, and great confusion.
For most of earth’s dwellers will perish by famine; and the sword will destroy the rest, who survive the famine.
The dead will be thrown out like dung, and there will be no one to console them; for the earth will be left a waste, and its cities thrown down.
There will be no one left to till the earth or sow it.
The trees will bear fruit, but who will gather it?
The grapes will ripen, but who will tread them? For in all places there will be great desolation.
Each will yearn just to catch sight of a fellow human, or to hear the sound of someone’s voice.
For ten will be left out of a city, and two out of the countryside, those who have hidden in the dense thickets and the clefts of the rocks.
Just as a few olives, three or four, remain on every tree of an olive grove,
or as in a vineyard that has been gathered some clusters are left by those who search the vineyard with care,
so in those days a remnant of three or four will escape the ones who comb through their houses sword in hand.
The earth will be left desolate, and its fields will grow old;{b} its roads and all its paths will sprout thorns, because no one will travel through it.
Virgins will mourn because they have no bridegrooms; women will mourn because they have no husbands; their daughters will mourn because they have no helpers.
Their bridegrooms will be destroyed in war, and their husbands will perish of famine.
But hear these things and understand them, you servants of the Lord.
See, here is the word of the Lord; receive it. Do not put your trust in the gods of whom the Lord speaks.{c}
See, the evils are drawing near and do not delay.

Just as a woman with child in her ninth month, when her time of delivery approaches, is seized two or three hours before by pangs that encircle her womb, and once the infant comes out there is not an instant’s pause,
so the evils will not linger in coming forth upon the earth; the world will groan, and pangs will grip it on every side.
“Listen to the word, my people: make ready for the fight, and amid the evils live as aliens in the land.
Let the seller be like one who flees, and the buyer like one who is about to lose;
let the merchant be like one who will get no profit, and the builder like one who will not live in the house;
let the sower be like one who will not reap, and the one who prunes the vine like one who will not gather the grapes;
let the ones who wed be as though they will beget no offspring, and the unwed as though bereaved.{d}
For this reason those who labor, labor in vain;
for strangers will reap their fruit, seize their goods, overturn their houses, and take their children captive; for in captivity and famine they bring forth their children.
And those who trade by robbery, the more they adorn their cities and houses, their property and their persons,
the more I will be angry with them for their sins, says the Lord.
Just as a harlot is jealous of a decent and very good woman,
so righteousness hates iniquity when she adorns herself, and accuses her to her face, when he comes who will defend the one who searches out every sin on earth.{e}
Therefore do not be like her or her works;
for in a very little while iniquity will be taken away from the earth, and righteousness will reign over you.
Let no sinner say that he has not sinned; for God will burn coals of fire{f} on the head of anyone who says, ‘I have not sinned before God and his glory.’
See, the Lord knows all the works of human beings, their devices, their thoughts, and their hearts.
For he said, ‘Let the earth be made,’ and it was made; ‘Let heaven be made,’ and it was made.
At his word the stars were fixed, and he knows the number of the stars.
He searches the abyss and its treasures; he has measured the sea and what it holds.
He has shut in the sea in the midst of the waters, and by his word he has hung the earth over the waters.
He spread out the heaven like a vault, and founded it upon the waters.
He placed springs of water in the desert, and pools on the tops of the mountains, to send down rivers from the lofty rock to water the earth.
He formed the human being, and put a heart in the midst of the body, and gave him breath, life, and understanding,
and the breath of God Almighty,{g} who made all things and searches out all hidden things in hidden places of the earth.
He knows your devices and what you plan in your hearts, when you sin and wish to hide your sins.
Therefore the Lord has thoroughly searched out all your works, and he will put you all to shame.
You will be confounded when your sins come forth before people, and your iniquities will be the accusers standing against you on that day.
What will you do? Or how will you hide your sins before God and his angels?
See, God is the judge; fear him. Leave off your sins, and forget your iniquities, never to commit them again; and God will lead you out and deliver you from every tribulation.
For see, the burning wrath of a great multitude is kindled against you; they will carry off some of you and feed you what has been sacrificed to idols.{h}
And those who consent to them will be held by them in derision and reproach, and trampled underfoot.
For in place after place, and in the neighboring cities, there will be a great uprising against those who fear the Lord.
They will be like madmen, sparing no one, plundering and laying waste those who still fear the Lord;
for they will lay waste and plunder their goods, and drive them out of their houses.
Then the testing of my chosen ones will be made plain, like gold tested by fire.
“Hear, my beloved ones, says the Lord: see, the days of tribulation are at hand, and I will deliver you from them.
Do not fear or doubt, for God is your guide.
You who keep my commandments and precepts, says the Lord God, do not let your sins weigh you down, or your iniquities lift themselves up over you.{i}

Woe to any held fast in the grip of their sins and smothered under their iniquities, like a field overgrown with brush whose path lies hidden under thorns, so that no one passes along it; it is closed off and handed over for the fire to devour.”

notes.text: Syria, the Greek and Latin name of the land north of Israel (Hebrew Aram); the name is probably shortened from “Assyria.”
Latin inveterabunt, “will grow old,” that is, lie fallow and go wild.
Latin ne diis credatis, “do not believe the gods,” perhaps a corruption; the sense may be “do not disbelieve what the Lord says.”
Compare 1 Corinthians 7:29–31.
The Latin of this verse is obscure.
Compare Psalm 140:10; Proverbs 25:22.
Latin spiramen, “breath,” recalling Genesis 2:7.

The persecution described in verses 69–74 seems to be of Christians compelled to eat food sacrificed to idols, as under the emperor Decius (AD 249–251), though the date is uncertain. Compare Acts 15:29; Revelation 2:14, 20.
The Latin of this verse is broken; the rendering follows the sense.
